item.title: Utah library confirms LGBTQ 'Pride' book for its 'smallest patrons' is kept easily accessible
item.description: The Provo City Library confirmed to Fox News Digital it includes "Pride is Love" and other LGBTQ board books in its collection, saying they are shelved among 2,500 titles.
item.content:encoded:
A Utah public library confirmed to Fox News Digital that an LGBTQ-themed children's book highlighted by a conservative outlet is part of its collection for its "smallest patrons" and is intentionally kept "central and easily accessible," while pushing back on claims that the book was on display.

"I can confirm that the library does own a copy of ‘Pride Is Love’ along with the other small board books that were pictured in the post you referenced," Carla Z. Gordon, director of library services at Provo City Library, told Fox News Digital in a statement Tuesday.

"They are not on display," Gordon added. "They are shelved in bins that contain over 2,500 other board books (any that are currently checked in). The post describes them as being 'central and easily accessible,' which is very true. These are books for our smallest patrons and we make them easy to find."

OREGON SCHOOL COUNSELOR FACES BACKLASH OVER 'CHOSEN FAMILY' BOOK FOR YOUTHS

On Monday, The Cougar Chronicle, which identifies itself as providing "independent conservative news and opinion at BYU," posted a photo of the book "Pride Is Love," with a caption that read, "EXCLUSIVE: The Provo City Library children's section is promoting radical gender theory, critical race theory, and other progressive propaganda to Provo's children."

The thread also included photos of other LGBTQ children's books, including titles such as "Pride Puppy!," "It's a They!," "My Two Dads and Me," and another called, "My Moms Love Me."

TRANSGENDER DOLLS TO BE AVAILABLE FOR MINNESOTA SCHOOLCHILDREN AS YOUNG AS 4 UNDER WALZ-BACKED PROGRAM: REPORT

The Amazon page for the book, "Pride is Love," says it is intended for babies through age three and is about a girl and her two dads as they prepare to march in a Pride parade.

Similarly, "My Two Dads and Me," is also intended for babies through age three and shows the day-to-day of LGBTQ fathers and their children through everyday routines, from breakfast and trips to the park, to bath time and bedtime.

WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE

In her statement, Gordon referenced a portion of the library’s website she said has been created to help parents select materials that match their family values.

Gordon also highlighted the library’s Selection Policy, which is to "collect, organize, and make easily available to the people of the community materials which will help them in the pursuit of education, information, and the creative use of leisure time."

"Within the limits of space and budget, the collection offers patrons materials in a choice of format, treatment, and level of difficulty," she added. "In this way, most individual library needs can be met and service provided to individuals of all ages."

PORTLAND PARENT FIGHTS CHILD'S ELEMENTARY SCHOOL OVER 'FINAL STRAW' OF ADDING TRANS-INCLUSIVE FLAG

"These particular books are not currently on display, but we do have many displays throughout the library that try to highlight books available," Gordon said. "We sometimes use holidays, observances, visiting authors, popular topics, and completely random themes all in attempt to promote our collections."

"As mentioned in the Selection Policy, we do try to represent differing perspectives on many topics," she added. "Gender, sexuality, and race are all topics that have a variety of perspectives, so we do own books representing those differing voices." 

"We do receive complaints from parents and community members about materials in the collection. The process is outlined in the policy referenced above," Gordon added. "When we receive these concerns, we review the materials and follow the process to either retain, move, or discard items."

Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, appeared to express concern about the situation in a Monday post on X, sharing the thread from The Cougar Chronicle and writing, "Come on, Provo You’re better than this."

item.title: Dolly Parton's ‘all-American heart’: How country icon forged special bond with US military
item.description: Dolly Parton's bond with the military included troop performances, patriotic art on a KC-135 Stratotanker and a fiery message to Saddam Hussein.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton wore rhinestones and fringe, not a military uniform, but the American music legend spent decades finding her own ways to serve those who served America.

Parton, who died Tuesday at 80 in Nashville, forged a lasting connection with the military during her seven-decade career.

Her iconic blonde likeness appeared on U.S. military aircraft, she performed for troops and military families, recorded patriotic music and once took the Grand Ole Opry stage as American service members watched from Iraq.

TRUMP MOURNS DOLLY PARTON, ORDERS US FLAGS LOWERED NATIONWIDE AFTER COUNTRY MUSIC ICON DIES

The connection was personal, too. Carl Dean, Parton's husband of nearly six decades, enlisted in the Army shortly after they began dating and served for two years, according to Biography.com. The couple married in 1966, and remained together until Dean's death in 2025.

Parton once described her patriotism in simple terms.

"I've got an all-American heart," she told Vanity Fair in a 1991 profile.

Vanity Fair accompanied Parton to Fort Hood, Texas, for that profile, where she met service members, including soldiers who had returned from the Persian Gulf only weeks earlier. The magazine also reported that Parton's likeness appeared on a KC-135 and an A-10 Thunderbolt during the Gulf War era.

During her Fort Hood visit, Parton climbed onto the shoulders of an Army major near two M-1 tanks and delivered a pointed message to Saddam Hussein in a way only she could.

COUNTRY STAR CHRIS JANSON SAYS RESPECTING THE FLAG IS THE NUMBER ONE LESSON HE WANTS HIS KIDS TO LEARN

"Saddam Hussein, you son of a b----!" Parton shouted, according to Vanity Fair. "You touch one of my men again and see what happens!"

Later, Parton posed for photographs with soldiers and their families and signed autographs inside a Fort Hood theater, the magazine reported.

The service members eventually began chanting: "Dol-ly! U-S-A! Dol-ly! U-S-A!"

More than a decade later, Parton's connection with the military produced another memorable tribute.

At a September 2004 event at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base in Tennessee, Parton unveiled patriotic nose art bearing her likeness on a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 134th Air Refueling Wing, according to an Air National Guard photo record preserved by the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service.

LEE GREENWOOD RECALLS SURVIVING ENEMY FIRE IN PANAMA AFTER WHITE HOUSE SENT HIM TO ENTERTAIN TROOPS

The aircraft was dubbed "Miss Dolly." Parton autographed the artwork and performed several songs for airmen and their families at the event.

The appearance followed the release of Parton's For God and Country on Veterans Day 2003. The album combined patriotic standards with original Parton songs.

"I’m not a bit political, but I’m extremely patriotic," Parton said of the album, according to her official website, as cited by Military.com.

Parton's music had addressed war and military families before that album. Military.com noted that her 1970 song "Daddy Won’t Be Home Anymore" concerned a mother preparing to tell her children their father had died at war, while "Welcome Home," from For God and Country, centered on a parent waiting for a son to return from overseas.

In April 2005, Parton performed during a Grand Ole Opry live broadcast in Nashville while U.S. troops watched by video feed from Iraq, according to DVIDS.

STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING

Then-Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld also joined Parton onstage. According to DVIDS, Rumsfeld visited Nashville to thank Parton, the Grand Ole Opry and the American people for supporting U.S. troops.

Parton's work with military families continued later in her career. She participated in a virtual USO program in December 2022 that allowed service members around the world and their families to speak with her and ask questions, according to Military.com.

Her Imagination Library also blessed military families. In 2024, the program's Washington affiliate partnered with the Government Employees Health Association on a $15,000 grant to expand free books for young children in military families, Military.com reported. The effort served families at Naval Base Kitsap, Joint Base Lewis-McChord and Naval Station Everett.

The military community was among those mourning Parton following her death Tuesday.

Boot Campaign, a nonprofit that works with veterans and military families, remembered Parton's support in a tribute posted to X.

"We are so heartbroken to hear of the passing of @DollyParton who used her platform to support so many, including Veterans, military families and our work at Boot Campaign," the organization wrote. "Rest in peace, Dolly."

The group accompanied the tribute with an image of Parton saluting while wearing camouflage pants and combat-style boots beneath the hashtag "#LaceUpAMERICA."

The official U.S. Marine Corps account offered an even simpler farewell Tuesday, sharing a photograph of Parton singing in camouflage.

"RIP Dolly Parton."

Parton's family said a small, private service will be held for immediate family at her request. Fans and friends around the world were encouraged to pay tribute to Parton on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at DollyParton.com.

In lieu of flowers, the family asked that donations be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library, the literacy program she founded in 1995.

item.title: Colin Kaepernick to receive Muhammad Ali Award for fighting 'racial injustice'
item.description: Colin Kaepernick will receive the Muhammad Ali Center's Humanitarian of the Year Award, but comparing his NFL anthem protest to Ali's sacrifices misses.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick will receive the Muhammad Ali Center’s Humanitarian of the Year Award later this year.

The center told Reuters that it selected Kaepernick for his advocacy "against racial injustice" and support for underserved communities through his Know Your Rights Camp and other philanthropic efforts.

Lonnie Ali, Muhammad’s late wife and co-founder of the center, added:

"Colin has used his platform to advocate for equality, human dignity, and social change, even when doing so came at significant personal and professional cost."

STOP COMPARING JAXSON DART'S NEW YORK TRUMP RALLY SPEECH TO COLIN KAEPERNICK'S ACTIVISM

Now, to reality.

Kaepernick is hardly worthy of an award bearing Muhammad Ali’s name. Ali risked his freedom and sacrificed the prime of his boxing career when he refused induction into the military during the Vietnam War. He was stripped of his heavyweight title, barred from boxing for more than three years and convicted of draft evasion.

Ali became a martyr. He paid a real price. Kaepernick did neither.

The popular narrative that Kaepernick sacrificed a thriving NFL career to stand up for marginalized communities is misleading. He had already been benched for Blaine Gabbert. In his final two seasons, he posted QBRs of 43.7 and 49.2.

VICTOR WEMBANYAMA CROSSING HIS ARMS DURING U.S. NATIONAL ANTHEM IS A PROBLEM FOR THE NBA

He had become unplayable.

Unlike Ali, Kaepernick was not on a battlefield alone. It was quite the opposite. Sports media and pop culture largely championed his national anthem protests. Nike made him the face of a major advertising campaign

Kneeling during the anthem proved financially rewarding for an athlete who would've had to otherwise settle for league minimum contracts.

Kaepernick and his defenders say the NFL blackballed him. In reality, no team wanted a backup-quality quarterback attached to a divisive political circus. Most players who kneeled during the anthem kept their jobs because their play warranted it. Kaepernick’s did not.

He had also become an inflammatory figure, denouncing July 4 as a racist celebration and comparing the NFL’s treatment of players to slavery and plantations.

Colin Kaepernick was more moron than martyr.

The Muhammad Ali Center should be ashamed to honor him. Then again, the center lost much of its prestige years ago. In 2022, it awarded Dr. Anthony Fauci its Lifetime Achievement Award.

Oh, how poorly that has aged.

Still, Kaepernick will use the award to promote his upcoming book, "The Perilous Fight."

item.title: Helicopter rescue crew caught on camera saving 2 climbers trapped along popular California beach cliff
item.description: Video shows a CHP helicopter crew hovering above a Big Sur ravine to hoist two climbers stranded 600 feet below the roadway at Hurricane Point.
item.content:encoded:
Two climbers in California stranded on a steep Big Sur cliffside Saturday found themselves 600 feet below the roadway with a California Highway Patrol (CHP) helicopter crew their only way out.

Video released by the CHP shows the H-70 helicopter hovering above a steep ravine near Hurricane Point as a rescue technician is lowered on a cable to reach the trapped pair.

Big Sur Fire requested help from CHP’s Paso Robles Air Unit at about 6:24 p.m., according to the agency.

NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS

The terrain was so steep that the technician could not safely disconnect from the hoist hook after reaching the first climber. Instead, he secured the climber in a Pelican rescue harness and the two were lifted together to rescue personnel waiting at a staging area.

The helicopter then returned to the ravine and carried out the same technical maneuver to bring the second climber to safety.

RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION

CHP did not release the climbers’ names or explain how they became stranded.

Social media users praised the CHP air crew and the rescue teams involved after video of the operation was posted online.

"Incredible rescue!! Well done guys!!" one commenter wrote. Another called it an "amazing job by all involved," while another added, "Just incredible, you guys, thanks for what you do!"

Both climbers survived the ordeal, authorities said.

HIKER AIRLIFTED AFTER TERRIFYING RATTLESNAKE BITE ON REMOTE TRAIL AS INCIDENTS SURGE IN AREA

"These high-risk, low-frequency rescues are exactly what CHP Air Operations personnel continuously train for," the agency said. "There is no room for error when operating in steep terrain, under hoist, and in challenging environmental conditions."

The cliffside rescue followed two separate Aug. 9 rescue missions for the same H-70 crew.

MISSING GRAND CANYON HIKER, 83, RESCUED AFTER GETTING SEPARATED FROM COMPANION

The air unit first hoisted an injured 13-year-old hiker from Pinnacles National Park, working with a Paso Robles Fire Department helicopter rescue technician, CHP said.

Later that day, the crew pulled a person who suffered severe injuries in a fall from a waterfall in Big Sur Gorge to safety.

H-70 then responded to another call in the remote Los Padres National Forest, where a hunter suffering from heat exhaustion and dehydration was brought aboard using a hover step-on maneuver and flown to waiting medics in King City.

item.title: US Olympic hero Nancy Hogshead launches petition calling for WNBA to restrict gender eligibility
item.description: Nancy Hogshead's Change.org petition has over 11,000 signatures demanding the WNBA clarify eligibility rules to explicitly include only biological females.
item.content:encoded:
Three-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Nancy Hogshead is calling on the WNBA to explicitly restrict player eligibility to biological females.

Hogshead recently launched a Change.org petition asking the league to clarify the meaning of "woman" in its eligibility rules. The petition has collected more than 11,000 signatures since its Aug. 14 launch.

"We’re calling for the WNBA to clarify that its eligibility rules are for women only," Hogshead told Fox News Digital. "If you wanna participate, you have to be a certain age, and you have to be a female."

CHARLES BARKLEY DECLARES WNBA IS 'FOR WOMEN ONLY' AFTER ONGOING TRANSGENDER ATHLETE DEBATE

Hogshead said she hopes the petition ultimately reaches 100,000 signatures.

"It’s an 80/20 issue across the country, so we can do it," she said. "We have well over a million people who’ve engaged with our materials that we put out about the petition. We just gotta get them to sign on."

The WNBA’s 2026 collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." However, the agreement does not further define "woman" or include specific language addressing gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

The debate intensified after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while claiming to identify as women. League sources hav since said that neither of them is eligible and characterized their announcements as "publicity stunts."

Hogshead said the declarations exposed what she considers a contradiction in policies based on gender self-identification.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT ON PROTECTING GIRLS FROM COMPETING AGAINST 'BIOLOGICAL MEN'

"I love it that they came forward because it just shows the hypocrisy of the WNBA, and it shows the hypocrisy of gender ideology," Hogshead said. "For them to come forward and, you know, threaten to play in the WNBA and show up for the draft, it just shows just how ridiculous that gender ideology is."

The WNBA previously said there were "no immediate eligibility matters" affecting the league and denounced "bad-faith efforts" to use the debate to "demean or marginalize others." Commissioner Cathy Engelbert also said league officials would continue discussing the subject with the players’ union and other stakeholders.

Hogshead’s petition comes amid rallies outside WNBA games supporting Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who publicly opposed transgender participation in girls’ and women’s sports earlier this summer.

"I really appreciate her for the stand that she has taken on behalf of women," Hogshead said of Cunningham. "If anything, the more people see of Sophie Cunningham, the more they like her."

Hogshead won three gold medals and one silver medal at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. She later became a civil rights attorney and founded Champion Women, an organization that advocates for women and girls in athletics.

item.title: Peyton Manning pays tribute to Dolly Parton: 'Tennessee won't be the same without her!'
item.description: Peyton Manning shared a heartfelt tribute to Dolly Parton, reflecting on their Tennessee connection and her iconic 2023 Vols "Rocky Top" performance.
item.content:encoded:
Tributes, condolences and more are pouring in after news of country music legend Dolly Parton’s death at 80 surfaced on Tuesday.

Among those was Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning, who shared a connection with Parton given their ties to Tennessee.

"There was only one Dolly and I feel lucky to have known her," Manning, who played his college football at the University of Tennessee, wrote in an Instagram post walking alongside Parton at a Vols game.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"We’ll miss you, Dolly. Tennessee won’t be the same without her!"

The picture that Manning posted was one of many iconic performances for Parton, but this one was exceptionally good by the East Tennessee native. She performed the Vols’ signature "Rocky Top" song after the first quarter on Nov. 18, 2023.

STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING

Parton even said that she could barely hear herself during her performance because the stadium was so loud. But Parton’s moments in sports went well beyond appearances at Vols games.

Just days after her performance in Knoxville, Parton was in Dallas at AT&T Stadium for a 2023 Thanksgiving performance, wearing a custom bedazzled Cowboys cheerleader outfit for the halftime show. She was 77 years old at the time, and rave reviews poured in about her country music ensemble, which included hits like "Jolene," "9 to 5," and even tossing in Queen’s iconic "We Are The Champions" track.

"Well at my age, if I can pull it off, it’s going to be good," Parton told USA TODAY about the performance, which she admitted being nervous for. "And if I don’t, I can just pass it off as an old woman doing a stupid thing. I’ve always said my desire to do something is greater than my fear of it."

Parton died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, on Tuesday, according to a press release obtained by Fox News Digital.

Her nephew, Brin Seaver, also revealed the news in an Instagram video, which comes after Parton spent months battling an unknown health issue.

Parton was much more than a country music artist, as she was known for also being an actress, a philanthropist, a businesswoman and humanitarian.

During her illustrious life and career, Parton tallied 11 Grammy Awards, three Emmy Awards, and the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award, while also being nominated for six Golden Globe Awards, a Tony Award and two Academy Awards.

Parton was also married to Carl Dean for nearly 60 years, with their relationship mostly remaining outside the public eye. Dean passed away in March 2025.

At Parton’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family.

In lieu of flowers, the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.

Fox News’ Christian Dugan Ramirez contributed to this report.

item.title: Clinton-appointed judge triggers appeal after blocking key voter citizenship law
item.description: Frank LaRose vows to appeal after a Clinton-appointed judge blocked Ohio's voter registration citizenship proof law, citing federal conflicts.
item.content:encoded:
A Clinton-appointed judge in Ohio is blocking the implementation of an Ohio law that requires voting registrants to provide photo ID proof of their citizenship before enrollment.

In a decision delivered on Tuesday, Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. stayed the law, citing what he saw as a conflict with federal requirements.

"The court grants plaintiff’s motion for preliminary injunction … from relying on House Bill 54’s amendment to require any driver’s license or renewal to produce documentary proof of citizenship before offering the opportunity to register to vote," Oliver wrote.

The decision is just the latest development in the national debate over state-level voting requirements designed to prevent non-citizens from participating in U.S. elections — and how far those requirements can go without overarching federal reforms. 

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT RESTORES TEXAS MAIL BALLOT ID REQUIREMENTS IN MAJOR ELECTION INTEGRITY RULING

Most immediately, the decision means that voter registrants in Ohio can once again enroll without a passport, a current driver’s license, a certification of naturalization, or a birth certificate.

Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose announced on Tuesday that his office plans to appeal the decision.

"We strongly disagree with that decision, and I’ve asked our legal team to file an immediate appeal. I will vigorously defend our legal authority to safeguard our voter rolls and protect the integrity of Ohio’s elections," LaRose said in a statement.

In the case of Red Wine & Blue v. the Ohio Secretary of State, the court was asked to weigh whether requirements under the new Ohio law conflict with the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA), also known as the "Motor Voter Act."

That law, passed in 1993 under the Clinton administration, instructs states to give voters the opportunity to register to vote using the same information they use when applying for a driver’s license. The bill was originally intended to increase voter participation.

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

It states that "the voter registration application portion … for a driver’s license may not require any information that duplicates information required in the driver’s license portion of the form."

Notably, the NVRA doesn’t explicitly prohibit states from requiring proof of citizenship. But because virtually all driver's license forms ask about citizenship status, Oliver believes further proof amounts to redundancy.

He laid out his view in Tuesday’s decision.

"As the rest of Ohio’s voter registration scheme demonstrates, election officials do not need documentary proof of citizenship to assess a voter registration applicant’s citizenship because signed attestation of citizenship is enough," Oliver wrote.

LaRose, the secretary of state, disagreed. He cited instances of known voter fraud that have escaped detection because of the current enforcement mechanisms.

MEXICAN NATIONAL CONVICTED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN US AFTER FALSE CITIZENSHIP CLAIMS FACES REMOVAL: DHS

"Earlier this year, an Ohio woman admitted to voting illegally as a lawful permanent resident in 2018 because, according to the judge in the case, ‘a [Bureau of Motor Vehicles] clerk, a government official, told her to register.’ The court found her not guilty by reason of entrapment. The judge specifically noted that the voter admitted she knew she was not a citizen when she voted, but he found that the BMV employee misled her into violating the law by implying she was eligible to vote."

"The Franklin County case proves it’s not enough to just have a person’s attestation," LaRose added. "Ohio has a constitutional requirement to ensure that only U.S. citizens are voting in our elections."

item.title: Female Virginia officer sues police department after allegedly sharing locker room with biological male
item.description: Former Norfolk police officer Meghan Grabow sued her police department earlier this month after sharing a women's changing room with a biological male in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
A former Norfolk, Virginia, police officer filed a lawsuit against the city and its police chief earlier this month after the police department allegedly allowed a biological male to use the women's locker rooms.

According to the documents obtained by Fox News Digital, the Aug. 10 legal complaint stemmed from an August 2024 incident in which former Norfolk police officer Meghan Grabow was changing in the women's locker room and stripped down to her underwear when a recruit described as a "biological male who identifies as a woman" entered the room wearing a suit and tie. Grabow said that the recruit looked at her "as a man would look at a woman" before moving to another part of the locker room.

Grabow claimed that when she spoke to her superiors about her discomfort, she was told to "learn to deal with it" and "find another locker room" if she was uncomfortable.

SAN FRANCISCO YMCA CHANGES LOCKER ROOM RULES AFTER TRANSGENDER CONTROVERSY: REPORT

In addition to this incident, Grabow said that she and other concerned officers were told by police chief Mark Talbot that the "woman" hired by the department "will use the restroom that's appropriate for her gender" and were repeatedly instructed to refer to the recruit as "she."

Other officers also voiced concerns that they were not warned about sharing facilities with a biological male, something Talbot acknowledged could have been handled "better."

APPEALS COURT REVIVES LAWSUIT BY ALASKA AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANTS FIRED AFTER OPPOSING PRIDE MESSAGE

Grabow later received an indefinite suspension pending termination in 2025 over a minor traffic violation committed prior to the incident after attempting to voice a complaint. Other officers have since left the department over their backlash to the transgender policy, the complaint states.

Grabow is seeking $15 million in compensatory damages, claiming Talbot and the police department were guilty of intentional infliction of emotional distress as well as violating her religious freedoms by forcing her to share a changing facility with a biological male and validate transgender ideology against her Catholic beliefs.

CHRISTIAN LIFEGUARD WHO REFUSED PRIDE FLAG DUTIES AND WAS SUSPENDED IS NOW HEADED TOWARD TRIAL

Attorney Scott Lloyd, who is representing Grabow in the case, told Fox News Digital in a statement that they are determined to protect female-only spaces through this case.

"We need to defend private spaces for the women who rely on them. Officer Grabow has done a brave and admirable thing by stepping forward, but it shouldn't have come to this," Lloyd said.

The Norfolk Police Department declined to comment to Fox News Digital, saying that it "cannot comment on pending litigation or personnel-related matters."

Under 2020 guidelines for the Norfolk Police Department, employees are encouraged not to question a transgender person's identity except for "articulable reasons," such as if they are related to a crime.

"Employees will respect an individual's gender identity and gender expression. An individual's gender expression may be traits that are not typically associated with a person's assigned sex at birth; these expressions may include wigs, prosthetics, makeup, adopted name, tone of voice, clothing, mannerisms, etc.," the 2020 general order read.

item.title: New research finds 1 in 4 NFL players could develop CTE in their lifetime: 'Should be a call to action'
item.description: A new study found at least one in four former NFL players may develop CTE, prompting Dr. Julian Bailes to call for urgent proactive brain protection.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL continues to make a concerted effort for safe play for all players, especially when it comes to head injuries.

But since chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, was found to be heavily linked to former professional football players, there has been ongoing discussion about how current and future NFL players could be affected.

New data published in The BMJ from a recent six-year research period provided some harrowing discoveries.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The study found that at least one in every four people who have played in the NFL might expect to end up with CTE at some point in their lives.

For the study, 878 former NFL players who died from 2016-21, which varied from players in their 20s to their 80s and in between, at least 215 of them had CTE in some stage.

That’s 24.5%, with the actual prevalence likely being higher considering there were 643 of those brains that were not examined.

ALDON SMITH'S FAMILY DONATING HIS BRAIN TO CTE RESEARCH AS ATTORNEYS INVESTIGATE DEATH

If these results were applied to the NFL today, which consists of 1,696 players on the active roster combined for all 32 teams — this doesn’t include practice squad players and those not on the roster due to other injury reasons — around 415 would be diagnosed with CTE.

One of the main problems of the degenerative brain disease is that it can only be confirmed as a diagnosis post-death once the brain is examined.

The neurodegenerative disease is caused by repeated blows to the head as well as severe head trauma. The symptoms found in those with CTE include memory loss, mood swings, erratic behavioral actions and more.

While the disease was first found in boxers, it has become associated with football players in this modern era due to the repeated blows to the head sustained on every snap of the ball. It has, however, also been found in athletes participating in hockey, rugby and other sports.

But its connection to football became public when beloved players like Junior Seau, Mike Webster, Frank Gifford and others were diagnosed with CTE after their deaths. Webster was dubbed "Patient Zero" after Dr. Bennet Omalu examined his brain and became the first to diagnose an NFL player with CTE, jump-starting a concussion crisis within the game.

Dr. Julian Bailes, a neurosurgeon and chief medical advisor for Q-30 Sports Science, has spent decades studying the disease as well as concussion and repetitive subconcussive impacts. He helped pioneer the early investigation into CTE, being portrayed by Alec Baldwin in the popular film, "Concussion." He has also authored more than 300 publications and previously advised the NFL Players Association, NCAA and Pop Warner Football.

Seeing this study, Dr. Bailes believes it "should be a call to action for everyone involved in football."

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION STEVE MCMICHAEL, WHO DIED LAST YEAR, REVEALED TO HAVE CTE

"We have made tremendous progress in recognizing and managing concussions, but the science increasingly tells us that diagnosed concussions are only part of the equation," Dr. Bailes said in a statement provided to OutKick. "Repetitive head impacts accumulated over years of play matter, and we need to bring the same urgency we’ve applied to understanding CTE to preventing and reducing the forces experienced by the brain in the first place.

"That means continuing to advance rules, training, equipment and new approaches to brain protection at every level of the game. This should not be approached as an all or nothing assignment. The next frontier in athlete safety must be proactive brain protection."

A simple proactive action would be eliminating repeated blows to the head, which researchers know prevents CTE. Obviously, the game of football would forever be changed and there’s much more complexities there, especially at the professional level.

"The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league told The Athletic in a statement. "The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being."

The NFL Players Association also told the outlet, "The finds should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem."

There were 168 documented in-game concussions during the 2025 NFL season, which was a 30% increase from the 129 record during the 2024 campaign. There were a total of 538 evaluations and 26 medical timeouts as well.

item.title: Newsom promises new legal fight after Trump gets Supreme Court victory on mail-in voting
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom says the state will sue again after the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling allowed Trump's mail-in voting restrictions.
item.content:encoded:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans to sue the Trump administration over its push to restrict mail-in voting after the Supreme Court allowed the administration to enforce challenged provisions of President Donald Trump’s executive order for "election integrity" while litigation continues.

The announcement sets up the next phase of the legal fight after the Supreme Court (SCOTUS) ruled 6-3 in favor of the Trump administration Monday, lifting an injunction that had blocked the order in 23 states ahead of November's midterm elections.

SCOTUS stressed that its decision addressed the injunction rather than the ultimate legality of the order, leaving the door open to additional challenges.

Newsom criticized the decision in a statement released by his office.

JACKSON RIPS INTO SUPREME COURT COLLEAGUES' 'SERIOUS LEGAL ERROR' ON TRUMP MAIL-IN VOTING ORDER

"The Supreme Court just let the Trump administration move ahead (for now) with its plan to disenfranchise voters across the country," Newsom said. "California will be suing AGAIN to block these Orwellian rules from being implemented."

Newsom’s office also highlighted two election-related bills moving through the California Legislature that the governor says would protect the state’s elections from interference.

According to the governor’s office, AB 282 would establish new felonies involving the seizure of ballots, election records or certified voting technology before election results are certified. SB 259 would establish criminal penalties for interfering with the delivery or return of mail-in ballots, including a felony carrying up to four years in prison in certain cases.

CALIFORNIA ACCUSED OF BLOCKING FEDERAL VOTER ROLL AUDIT AS DOJ ESCALATES PROBE OF ELECTION FRAUD CLAIMS

The governor’s office described the measures as an "Election Protection" package and said they build on election-related legislation Newsom signed earlier this summer.

The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) and Department of Justice said they would move to implement the revised mail-ballot restrictions following Monday’s ruling.

Trump’s executive order directs federal agencies to compile citizenship-based lists of eligible voters and directs the USPS to deliver mail-in ballots only to people appearing on approved lists.

USPS WOULDN'T DELIVER BALLOTS IN STATES THAT REFUSE TO FORK OVER MAIL-IN VOTER INFO UNDER PROPOSED RULE

In explaining its decision, the Supreme Court concluded that the challenged provision directing the Department of Homeland Security to create and distribute state citizenship lists imposed obligations on federal agencies rather than the states themselves.

The court wrote:

"[It] directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to take appropriate action to create and distribute State Citizenship Lists. This provision is an internal directive from the President to a subordinate. It imposes no obligations on the States, so they ‘suffer no concrete harm from’ it, and without concrete harm, there is no standing."

Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented.

A representative for Newsom did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: DHS issues scathing rebuke after former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms touts cutting ties with ICE
item.description: Georgia gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms touted cutting ties with ICE as Atlanta mayor, prompting DHS to fire back with mugshots of criminals arrested in the city.
item.content:encoded:
Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms highlighted her past move to cut ties with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in 2018 as mayor of Atlanta, prompting a strong rebuke from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on Monday.

As Bottoms gave the keynote speech at a Democratic fundraiser in Dalton, Georgia, the former Biden official, now running for governor in the Peach State, spoke about refusing to cooperate with ICE during President Donald Trump’s first term.

In her speech, she recalled her musician father’s struggle with addiction, saying that her first tour around Georgia was visiting him at various prisons. She said this helped teach her the value of "seeing the humanity in people" even those who have made mistakes or "had a different pathway to this country."

"When I was mayor of Atlanta, when ICE had the family separation policy in our state, in our nation, I made the decision to end our multi-year, multi-million dollar agreement with ICE because all money ain’t good money," Bottoms said. "And when we did that, other cities followed, counties followed, other states followed and it made a difference."

DEMOCRAT MAYOR BLASTED BY DHS FOR 'HUNTING DOWN' PROPERTY OWNERS LEASING TO ICE: 'UNHINGED'

Fox News Digital reached out to DHS, and the department offered a scathing response to her statement.

"The only difference this anti-law enforcement, pro-criminal illegal alien, former mayor made was to obstruct federal immigration laws, making Atlanta-area communities a hotbed for illegal immigration on her watch," a spokesperson for DHS said.

"ICE does not separate families. Parents are asked if they want to be removed with their children or ICE will place the children with a safe person the parent designates," the statement continued. "This is consistent with past administration’s immigration enforcement."

"Parents can take control of their departure with the CBP Home app and reserve the chance to come back the right legal way," the spokesperson added. "The United States is offering illegal aliens $2,600 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return."

NEW YORK SHERIFFS 'MAD AS HELL' AS HOCHUL PUSHES TO BAN KEY LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERSHIP

The spokesperson made the case that cooperating with ICE is commonsense policy.

"Seven of the top ten safest cities in the United States cooperate with ICE," the official continued. "Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country. We have had tremendous success when local law enforcement work with us, including 40,000 arrests in Florida and a two-week operation in West Virginia that resulted in the arrest of over 650 illegal aliens."

"When politicians bar local law enforcement from working with DHS, our law enforcement officers have to have a more visible presence so that we can find and apprehend the criminals let out of jails and back into communities," the statement added.

EXCLUSIVE: ICE NABS MULTIPLE CONVICTED KILLERS IN SINGLE DAY AMID NATIONWIDE IMMIGRATION SWEEP

The spokesperson shared mugshots of illegal aliens arrested in Atlanta for crimes ranging from "strongarm rape" and sexual offenses toward a child to "threat-terroristic state offenses."

item.title: Ohio State coach Ryan Day addresses NFL players returning to college football: 'We're in a different world'
item.description: Ohio State's Ryan Day calls on conferences to establish a roster lock deadline as former NFL players become eligible to play college football.
item.content:encoded:
Not everything about modern college football is perfect, but we can say this for it: it's never boring.

After an offseason dominated by debate over the importance of strength of schedule and how it's defined, the changing of the guard between the SEC and Big Ten, potential involvement from the federal government in collegiate athletics, and even more NIL (name, image and likeness) concerns, there's now a new controversy, just a few days before the season starts.

Thanks to a series of cases making their way through the courts as a result of the NCAA adding a fifth year of eligibility, several players who ended their "amateur" careers and went to the NFL are now eligible to return to the college football ranks.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

Immediately, opportunistic coaches seized on the opportunity to add more physically developed and experienced players to their rosters. Led by new LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin.

This has led to a flood of conference calls and meetings among major conferences as to the propriety of players who signed with NFL teams being allowed to play college football. One of the most prominent voices in the sport, Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day, added his perspective, highlighting the push and pull of factors dominating discussion.

LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES

"I told myself I would stop saying this is crazy," Day told the media earlier this week. "So I’m not gonna say that. But to think that we’re in a situation where we’re this late in the season and our rosters are not locked in is frustrating at the very least. But I’m not gonna sit here and keep saying that. So what does that mean for us? That’s the bottom line. Well, I think, in my opinion, the conferences have to decide if there’s a point where their rosters have to be locked in. Because once some of these guys become available, adding them to the roster is going to provide advantage for certain teams. So we’re certainly having conversations. I’ve had conversations with Tony Petitti about this. I know he’s all over it and trying to do what’s best for the conference."

Those are all valid points. Rosters not being "locked in" with literally days to go before kickoff is not only crazy, it's unfair to the current players who could now be forced to compete for jobs with players who have experience in NFL training camps. Still, Day brought up that programs will have to "consider it" in order to keep up with other top teams.

NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE

"But we also, if there are teams that have some players out there who are cut from NFL rosters that are gonna be on other teams, we have to at least consider it and look at it," he added. "Do I like anything about it? Absolutely not, but we gotta do what’s right for Ohio State. So it’s sort of a day-to-day thing right now. And like anything, we’re just gonna try to adapt. But I think we would all agree, maybe not everybody, but that there has to be a certain point where your roster gets locked in."

That's the reality; if peer schools are signing NFL players, and you're not, you're falling behind. Just like you would fall behind if you're signing the 50th best recruiting class and Michigan is signing the number one recruiting class in the country. Or if you're not utilizing the transfer portal or NIL as efficiently as possible.

None of that changes the fact that it's bizarre, absurd, and ridiculous for players who have signed NFL contracts to return to college football. Which Day also acknowledged, referencing the recent headlines of Kiffin's LSU team bringing in a tight end for an NFL team.

"Whenever I heard that we were in a meeting and someone says, 'Yeah, LSU just got a commitment from the Browns’ tight end,' I said, 'we are definitely in a different world right now,'" he concluded.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

That's the reality, and it's hard to stomach. We are in a different world with college football, and it's going to take strong, consistent leadership to ensure it doesn't go too far. The bad news? As the past few years have repeatedly demonstrated, college football has anything but.

item.title: IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix may have been 'once-in-a-lifetime,' but this is why it needs to happen again
item.description: The Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C., delivered a once-in-a-lifetime spectacle with the Capitol and Washington Monument as backdrops.
item.content:encoded:
I still remember exactly where I was in late January when I got a message from an editor that President Trump was preparing to sign an executive order to bring an IndyCar race to Washington, DC.

I replied that there was no way it would happen during the 2026 season, which was only about a month away from starting at the time. The track needed to be designed, built and made safe before cars could get on it, not to mention all of the fan areas and other logistics.

But seven months later, I was on a plane to the nation's capital to see the Freedom 250 Grand Prix for myself, and, man, was I ever wrong.

WORLD CUP ENERGY CARRIES INTO FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX AS GLOBAL FANS CELEBRATE AMERICA'S HISTORIC BIRTHDAY

Not only did it work, but it was the once-in-a-lifetime spectacle it promised to be.

And, if there's any way, it needs to happen again.

For starters, there's really never been a backdrop like it. It was pretty awe-inspiring to see the Capitol and the Washington Monument towering over the circuit and to see every rooftop and terrace lined with people trying to get a view of the track.

The turnout on both days was incredible, and that, of course, is largely due to the fact that tickets were free. It was an unbeatable deal, even if the merch was not the cheapest I've ever seen.

I bought an event poster that I thought would be like $10, and it was $60 because it was printed on canvas.

That said, the food was fairly affordable, with the priciest thing I saw being a crab cake sandwich for $25. It's not a deal, but you won't have to skip a mortgage payment for a burger like you might at an F1 race.

One critique would be that they needed more screens around the track. Especially when you consider the nature of a street circuit, you really can't have too many screens. I believe I counted four in the one fan area on the National Mall, and none if you were watching from the outside part of the track.

That's a bit of a problem, because as anyone who has been to a street race can tell you, it can sometimes be hard to see a lot of the track.

There also wasn't a ton to do in the way of fan activations as you see at a lot of other races, but you could access the museums within the track, including the National Air and Space Museum.

I spent a good chunk of time in the fan area on the National Mall walking around and talking to fans, and it almost had a county fair vibe to it, which I mean in the best way possible.

Everyone I encountered seemed happy to be there, and I never saw politics come up once. In fact, most of the people OutKick's Jon Root and I talked to were happy that politics were taking a backseat to good old-fashioned American pride and racing, a sentiment shared by fans we spoke to from as far away as the UK and Norway.

If the monuments, landmarks, flyovers, and racing couldn't make you proud to live in the United States, I'm not sure anything could.

TRUMP TAKES HONORARY LAP AROUND INDYCAR TRACK IN WASHINGTON AHEAD OF FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX

Some fans we spoke to admitted that they didn't have the first clue about IndyCar, and I think that may be one of the greatest victories of this event for the series.

Nothing will get someone hooked on motorsports faster than attending a race. It’s hard to explain to nonfans why those of us who love the sport spend most Sundays watching cars go in circles.

You can explain strategies, technology and how important a battle for P8 in the standings is, but it just won't click.

But if you take someone to a race and they can see the cars, hear the cars and even smell, in this case, the Firestone rubber getting left behind on Pennsylvania Avenue, well, that's going to make them a fan faster than any broadcast ever could.

That was the experience thousands of people got on Sunday. They may not have taken the Metro out of DC talking about whether or not Scott McLaughlin should've gone for the race-winning move into Turn 1 on a restart with 20 laps left (I think he should've slipstreamed down Pennsylvania Ave. and tried into Turn 2), but they will, without a doubt, tune into races in the future.

The track itself turned out to be great, something I was not expecting. When it was unveiled, I remember being pretty underwhelmed by its seven corners, all but one of which was 90 degrees or close to it.

However, the early maps didn't make it clear that Turn 6 was one heck of a chicane, and the bumpy street circuit proved to be a challenge for drivers.

And, on top of that, overtaking was possible.

Plus, despite Kyle Kirkwood dominating the weekend, I thought the race was really entertaining. We got a good strategic battle with the frontrunners using the early caution to pull off a three-stopper, and the late cautions giving us some important restarts.

That extra race distance was a good call, and I'm sure everyone there went home feeling like they got their money's worth... even if their ticket was free.

The free tickets to the Freedom 250 Grand Prix were one of the coolest parts of the event, but if it's going to become a sustainable addition to the IndyCar calendar, that might need to change.

The city showed that it was capable of making it all work from a logistical perspective, but ticket revenue sure would help keep the lights on.

They did charge for premium ticket options, which helped pay for part of the event, with Penske Corporation paying for the rest. That means no taxpayer dollars were involved (sorry, Adam Schiff!).

Everything else was general admission, including the grandstands, which were first-come, first-served.

I think the solution would be to add a grandstand or two and charge standard IndyCar ticket prices to sit in those seats, but then maybe hold another free ticket lottery that lets people get in and watch from trackside.

While there may be a few details that would need a second look if the powers that be decide to run it back with Freedom 250 Grand Prix 2.0, I was really impressed by how smoothly everything went.

If IndyCar never hits the streets of Washington again, it will be really neat to tell people that you were there to see it happen.

But the event has the makings of a signature IndyCar race on a big scale, and that’s something the series needs. That’s what gets eyeballs on the sport and converts people into fans, as was on display this weekend.

Imagine a schedule with marquee races like the Grand Prix of Arlington, the Grand Prix of Long Beach, the Indianapolis 500 and a race around Washington, D.C.?

That would be something to behold and, given the reception, perhaps someday soon we’ll get to see it.

item.title: Massive fishing boat runs aground at popular beach with 1,000 gallons of diesel on board
item.description: A 58-foot fishing boat ran aground at North Beach in Northern California's Point Reyes National Seashore, triggering a closure and diesel removal effort.
item.content:encoded:
A 58-foot fishing boat ran aground at a popular Northern California beach — prompting a closure as crews worked to remove roughly 1,000 gallons of diesel from the vessel.

The Lake Bay became stranded early Friday at North Beach in Point Reyes National Seashore, according to an alert from the National Park Service (NPS).

The boat was carrying 40,000 pounds of squid at the time, Inverness resident Richard James told the Point Reyes Light, a local newspaper, citing a conversation with the vessel's skipper.

TSUNAMI OF SEWAGE FROM MEXICO BARRELS TOWARD US COASTLINE, OFFICIALS WARN

As crews began responding to the grounding, the park service announced the temporary closing of North Beach and North Beach Road.

No injuries, fuel leaks or impacts to wildlife were reported, the agency said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the NPS for further comment and details.

The Lake Bay can hold up to 2,800 gallons of fuel. It was reported to have approximately 1,000 gallons of diesel on board, according to a press release from the U.S. Coast Guard.

Crews were coordinating with the party responsible for the vessel and a contracted salvage company to remove the fuel, the Coast Guard said.

75-FOOT BOAT SURFS WAVE, RUNS AGROUND IN HAWAII

Capt. Jack Moran, owner of Sea Tow Cape May in New Jersey, told Fox News Digital that access and timing can pose challenges when dealing with a grounded vessel. 

"The biggest thing is going to be accessibility," Moran said, noting that crews have to contend with tides, currents and changing conditions. "Time is the enemy. You want to try and get it off there as quickly as possible." (He is not connected to or involved with the Lake Bay fishing boat.) 

With 40,000 pounds of squid reportedly onboard, Moran said removing the catch could present another challenge.

"Moving a product like that is challenging at a dock, let alone removing squid from a boat on a beach," he said.

For the Coast Guard, safety and environmental concerns remained at the center of the response.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Our top priorities are ensuring the safety of the first responders and the public, stabilizing the incident, and limiting environmental impacts," Lt. Cmdr. Carey Lewis, the Coast Guard incident commander, said in the release. 

"Responders are continuously monitoring and evaluating the site for pollution and any potential risk factors so we can approach operations with [an] intention to minimize environmental impacts."

The National Park Service asked visitors to stay away from North Beach while the closure is in effect to allow first responders to work safely.

The cause of the grounding remains under investigation, the Coast Guard said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Fox News Digital previously reported on another grounding in April involving a small cruise ship near Monuriki Island in Fiji, where the Tom Hanks movie "Cast Away" was filmed.

The Blue Lagoon Cruises vessel struck a reef after worsening weather caused its anchor to drag.

A high-speed ferry arrived around dawn to assist with the evacuation, allowing all passengers and non-essential crew members to leave the stranded ship with their belongings.

Passengers were taken back to Port Denarau, where the cruise line arranged hotel accommodations and alternative activities. No injuries were reported among passengers or crew.

Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Charles Barkley says WNBA players 'just don't like' Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham
item.description: Charles Barkley says WNBA players dislike Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham, blaming a mix of jealousy, race, and sexuality for the hostility.
item.content:encoded:
Charles Barkley didn’t mince words while talking about Indiana Fever stars Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and the WNBA.

"Those girls do not like Caitlin Clark or Sophie Cunningham," Barkley said, referring to the other players in the WNBA and their feelings toward two of the league’s most popular players. But Barkley didn’t think it was all about race.

"Without regard for race, they just don’t like them," Barkley added.

Barkley made those comments on "The Michael Smerconish Program" while the two discussed what Barkley called the WNBA’s "awful year." One of the incidents the pair talked about was DiJonai Carrington’s Flagrant 2 foul on Cunningham during the Aug. 8 game between the Fever and Chicago Sky.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Carrington delivered a vicious blow to Cunningham's head as the Fever guard attempted a fast-break layup. Cunningham was left with a bloody mouth following the contact. Referees reviewed the play, upgraded the call from a Flagrant 1 to a Flagrant 2 and ejected Carrington.

Shortly after her ejection, Carrington posted "WHITE PRIVILEGE" on social media and tagged the Fever. She later said she never claimed the Flagrant 2 itself was the result of white privilege, though she didn't explain what prompted the post.

Cunningham called the foul "unnecessary," said she had "no beef" with Carrington, then called it intentional and accused Carrington of seeking attention.

Smerconish said he went looking for data on whether hard fouls between Black and White WNBA players occur more often than they should. He said he found a peer-reviewed study suggesting they happen at the rate one would expect, which led him to argue that the media is what turns those incidents into racial controversies.

Barkley didn’t buy it.

"No, no, you’re wrong, though," Barkley said. "The reason they made it black and white [was] when that girl tweeted ‘white privilege.’ That was stupid on her part."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT AGAINST DIJONAI CARRINGTON AFTER FLAGRANT FOUL AND 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' POST

Barkley called it "a dirty play. Period." He said Carrington’s post turned it into a racial argument.

"When you turn stuff to the internet, all the race hustlers start coming out. We have a ton of race hustlers out there, White and Black. Let me repeat that. White and Black," Barkley said.

Smerconish then brought up Larry Bird and Magic Johnson, whose rivalry came with obvious racial undertones but helped turn the NBA into a massive national product. Barkley agreed those undertones existed. He said the difference was that Bird and Johnson respected each other.

"There was always respect," Barkley said, before repeating himself for emphasis. "There was always respect."

Barkley didn't accuse Carrington, or any other WNBA player, of racism. He did, however, offer his own theory for the hostility toward Clark and Cunningham.

"I’m not gonna get on here and call somebody a racist because I don’t have any proof," Barkley said. "Whether it’s race, sexuality, or whatever, there’s something going on there."

He said Clark and Cunningham are simply good players, but he believes the resentment toward them comes from a mix of factors.

"She’s just a really good basketball player. Same thing with Sophie. She’s a good player," Barkley said. "I think it has something to do with sexuality, race, and jealousy. I think it’s all three of them. I don’t know how you break up the percentages."

Barkley said the WNBA’s bad publicity bothers him because he believes the league has a lot going for it. The WNBA is expanding, players are making more money under a new CBA, and the league has young stars who should be driving the conversation.

Instead, Barkley said, the WNBA keeps finding itself wrapped up in hard fouls, social-media posts and arguments that have little to do with basketball.

Smerconish suggested the WNBA could benefit from the attention, invoking the old belief that there is no such thing as bad publicity. Barkley didn’t agree.

"I don’t think it works like that anymore, Michael," Barkley said. "When’s the last time you heard something positive about the WNBA? I can’t even remember."

item.title: Kyle Shanahan breaks 49ers silence on Jed York arrest, says he still has 'respect' for the club owner
item.description: Kyle Shanahan says Jed York's arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting has no effect on the San Francisco 49ers as a team heading into the season.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers said they weren't going to comment about owner Jed York getting caught up in a prostitution sting over the weekend because the legal matter is closed , but that policy collapsed in coach Kyle Shanahan's first press conference since the incident.

Shanahan became the first 49ers official to face questions, and he felt obliged to provide answers.

(Dude is a saint).

Shanahan said York's arrest and ensuing no-contest plea to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools charges in a deal with an Ohio prosecutor has no effect on the Bay Area football team.

MORE DETAILS EMERGE ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN PROSTITUTION STING

"My view is, as the coach, does it have effect on us as a team?" Shanahan said. "And that's what I continue to answer on from a football standpoint. It has no effect on us. I mean, as far as what we do day to day, what we talk about, it hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today. It doesn't have to do with what happens on the field."

Shanahan, who was involved in a head-on collision in July that affected how much he was on the field early in training camp, doesn't believe that or York's legal trouble will distract the football team in the upcoming season.

"Well, the one thing that went on yesterday I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team.

"So I think it's been training camp as usual."

49ERS COACH KYLE SHANAHAN ADMITS HE CAUSED CAR CRASH AFTER TAKING EYES OFF ROAD TO FIND HIS PHONE

This, of course, is a head coach's spin on an uncomfortable situation. The majority owner of the team spent a day in jail and was splashed across national headlines because, police documents say, he went on a website in Ohio and tried to enlist the services of a prostitute on Sunday.

Three times.

And he got caught because what he was actually doing was connecting with an operation run by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which arrested him with the help of East Palestine police.

NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK

Despite those details, Shanahan said he has not changed his opinion about the club's owner or his family.

"Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan admitted after saying he has spoken to York the last two days. "I mean, the views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that.

"But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it being a personal [matter], I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way."

Danielle Belluomini is York's wife of 15 years, but even the marriage has become a newsworthy drama. Multiple reports have cited a divorce petition filed by York almost four months ago with the reason for the break being "irreconcilable differences."

NFL owners are scheduled to gather on Wednesday to vote on the sale of the Seattle Seahawks and the York situation will almost definitely be discussed in some capacity. The league released a statement on Monday saying it is aware of York's situation, and he is subject to discipline under its Personal Conduct Policy.

So, whether Shanahan admits it or not, the football team could be affected if York is disciplined and that rises to a suspension or even removal — the latter of which is not likely but cannot be ruled out.

None of that is a concern right now for the coach, and he believes his players aren't moved by the publicity of York's troubles.

"That's what these guys deal with their whole careers," Shanahan said. "I got cameras on all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games, when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened.

"I feel something like this is actually easier for them than some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle of things that are more personal to themselves."

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom, deemed to have ‘the potential to be a threat,’ barred from Sky arena after altercation
item.description: Chicago Sky team owner Michael Alter said Tuesday Enes Kanter Freedom is barred from Wintrust Arena after his altercation with Natasha Cloud on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Sky team owner Michael Alter said Tuesday Enes Kanter Freedom is barred from Wintrust Arena after his altercation with Natasha Cloud on Sunday.

Alter made the comments in an address to beat writers.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"He has demonstrated to us, unequivocally, that he has the potential to be a threat," Alter said, via ESPN.

It’s unclear how Freedom was determined to be a "threat" and whether there are actions he could take to possibly clear himself as such. OutKick reached out to the Sky for further comment.

The incident occurred in the third quarter of the Sky’s loss to the Indiana Fever. Cloud scored a bucket that led to the Fever calling a timeout. She directed her emotion toward Freedom, who was sitting near the basket at the Wintrust Arena. Freedom stood up and walked toward Cloud. Sky players and security had to get in between the two.

Freedom was then escorted out of the arena and was unable to return for the rest of the game.

He explained the situation to OutKick after the game.

"Sophie Cunningham shot a three, and I put my hands up to celebrate," Freedom said. "Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’

"And I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her.’ And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me, and literally I just got up, and then I was like, ‘I’m just here to protect women, and that’s all.’"

Freedom was wearing a shirt that explained the definition of a woman. He said he believed the shirt contributed to Cloud’s outburst.

"I was cheering for my friend Sophie because when she shot that three, I put my hands in the air," Freedom said. "A couple possessions later, she came back and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’ And I was shocked. I was like, ‘Listen, I’m not trying to sleep with her. I think she’s awesome. She’s a good friend.’ But I think it has a lot to do with my shirt.

"I was obviously wearing a shirt explaining what a woman is, and I think that had a lot to do with what she thinks about women. I think it triggered her a lot."

Alter said Tuesday that Freedom began "chirping" at Cloud in the third quarter.

"He began to chirp with her in the third quarter," Alter said, via Chicago State of Mind Sports. I would characterize it as trash talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention, engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her.

OutKick reached out to Freedom's reps for a response to the Sky's decision.

Cloud didn’t speak at the Sky’s postgame media availability. She fired off a message on Threads in support of the transgender community.

"To every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me," Cloud wrote.

Cloud’s message appeared to be a swipe at Freedom, who announced his intentions to compete in the WNBA as players and coaches have spoken out about trans athletes in women and girls’ sports. Freedom was wearing a T-shirt with the definition of a woman on it.
